A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 32-page versions of the same Mamba-HoME paper. The main text, equations, 26 tables, 12 figures, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original segmentation experiments, PDAC detection results, architecture ablations, and cross-modal evaluations in Section 3 and Appendices C–F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports revised numerical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The grouped slot assignment, two-level expert routing, Mamba backbone, GSC, Dynamic Tanh, decoder, and training loss are retained. Revised expert indices, flattened slot notation, and MLP labels clarify existing operations without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use AbdomenAtlas and TotalSegmentator MRI for pre-training and PANORAMA, AMOS, FeTA, MVSeg, and in-house CT for downstream evaluation. The same transfer and joint-training scenarios remain. Figure 12 corrects its description of fetal MRI fine-tuning, which was already documented elsewhere in v2.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: VoCo-B, Hermes, Swin SMT, VSmTrans, uC 3DU-Net, Swin UNETR, SegMamba, and SuPreM. The exclusion of VoCo-B from AMOS comparisons already appears in v2.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 substantively revises boundary-error evaluation: HD95 becomes the maximum of directional 95th-percentile surface distances, and mHD95 explicitly averages class-specific case means. This changes a central metric across the evaluations. Dataset splits and epoch budgets are retained; the PDFs do not establish that training was rerun.

E4.justification: The retained expert-count, group-size, slot-count, and normalization ablations receive revised quantitative evidence. For example, Table 8 changes FeTA LN/DyT scores from 87.6/87.7 to 87.5/87.4, reversing their small relative difference. No new ablation question or qualitative case study is introduced.

E5.justification: v2 reports ± values alongside segmentation results throughout Tables 11–26; v3 removes them from all these benchmark, ablation, and generalizability tables without replacement uncertainty estimates. The five-fold FeTA evaluation and Wilcoxon p < 0.05 statement remain unchanged. No additional seed or repeated-run information is provided.

E6.justification: Boundary scores change extensively in Tables 1, 2, 4 and the appendices. In Table 2, AMOS-CT mHD95 changes from 32.0 to 12.2 mm for pretrained Mamba-HoME and from 40.5 to 11.3 mm for Hermes, reversing their ranking. Several DSC and ablation entries also change. The revised HD95 scores accompany a changed metric definition and cannot establish same-setting model improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix B.3 replaces v2’s percentile over already-maximized Hausdorff distances with directional distance distributions and their percentiles, and formalizes averaging over cases where each class is present. This is a substantive mathematical correction confined to evaluation; the model equations otherwise receive notation changes and renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning hierarchical routing, efficient long-context modeling, segmentation performance, and generalization across CT, MRI, and ultrasound.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 newly explains Gaussian weighting as reducing patch-boundary artifacts and motivates augmentations through fetal motion, anatomical variability, and ultrasound noise. The main interpretations and limitations concerning larger datasets and self-supervised learning are retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents pre-training and PANORAMA augmentations, additional training/inference patch details, H100 80GB memory, binary-erosion surface extraction, and inference timing boundaries and warm-up. It omits the earlier pre-training sliding-window overlap description. These are documentation changes rather than demonstrated changes to the underlying experiments; code access remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive positioning relative to Mamba, Soft MoE, SegMamba, and earlier medical segmentation methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendices A and B undergo extensive prose rewriting, accompanied by widespread caption revisions and rewritten generalizability explanations. Expert notation and terminology are standardized. The section hierarchy and overall argument remain intact.

P2.justification: Appendix tables are substantially reformatted: two-block AMOS tables, including Tables 15, 18, 21, and 23–26, become single wide tables. Headers, column ordering, captions, and spacing change, including reversed PDAC/pancreas HD95 columns in Table 11. Figure 1 is slightly adjusted; qualitative image panels are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the HD95 mathematics, adds useful implementation details, and reconciles several repeated ablation/reference rows. However, removing the variability values throughout Tables 11–26 substantially reduces statistical transparency. These gains in correctness and documentation coexist with a meaningful loss of evidence about variability, preventing a reliable overall net-quality judgment.
